action_items: User must redeploy https://thevanguardnetwork.com/ to pick up the improved exception-handler (server.py) and any frontend changes — production is still running the older code that returns the generic 'Could not save your response. Please try again.' message. No code fix required from our side; this is a deployment action for the user.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L1333–1338: exception detail is now surfaced to the client — good for debuggability. Consider capping the total response length and/or scrubbing service-account paths from stack messages before returning to the browser, in case gspread raises with a file path in str(e). Currently str(e)[:200] is a reasonable guard.

Observed pre-existing quirk (not a regression of this iteration): consecutive automated POSTs to /api/nominate-decline/submit within a few seconds all land in the same row (row 31 kept getting overwritten in rapid-fire tests). Real user submissions (rows 26–30 in the sheet) stack correctly since they arrive minutes/hours apart. Likely a gspread/Sheets append_row 'table range' inference issue with USER_ENTERED input on rapid successive writes. Non-blocking for real user flow, but worth investigating if we ever add automated batch imports.

rca of the issue: Root cause of user-reported bug: production deployment at thevanguardnetwork.com is running an older bundle of /api/nominate-decline/submit that pre-dates the current code (the older code returns a generic 'Could not save your response. Please try again.' with no detail). The preview endpoint (current code) writes to Google Sheets correctly and returns {ok:true, row_id:'sheet-row-N'}; when it fails it now returns 'Could not save your response (ClassName: message).' — verified in /app/backend/server.py L1333–1338. Reproduction: POST to preview URL succeeds (confirmed row landed in DECLINES sheet). Mitigation: user must redeploy production. No code change required.
